title: The limit-approximation introduction omits a stage quantifier and drops the word limit.
details: Marks, dated 2024-02-25, §16.2 printed p. 69 (PDF69), paragraph before Definition 16.12 and paragraph before Theorem 16.13. Both visually checked. In the positive-membership branch of the pointwise limit definition, the stage s is free: the needed condition is, for eachx inA, there exists a stage s such that every later approximation containsx; use the analogous eventual exclusion when x is outsideA. Later the text concludes that every co-c.e. set is computable. The complement of K is a counterexample. The given construction instead proves that every co-c.e. set is limit computable. Both are local wording/quantifier slips; the adjacent limit lemma retains its intended meaning. Its proof also needs finite approximations to restrict x≤s if the approximating sets are required finite. Roadmap only; no current consumer.
